review_type: Independent internal mathematical and final-prose review; not external peer review or empirical validation
verdict: No blocking mathematical or inference defect found under the stated conditions
checked_assumptions: Fixed supported target policy and observation law, or conditioning on an independently trained policy held fixed for evaluation.
Exact assignment mechanisms and coherent V(Q) computed from the same Q; the arbitrary-Q mean identity is assumed from the main identification result.
Iid independent root clusters with a fixed prespecified trajectory count, equal root averaging and arbitrary permitted dependence inside a root.
A fixed finite number of folds formed independently of root data; fold proportions have positive limits; fitting and tuning exclude complete evaluation roots.
Fold-specific training information includes independent learner randomness; foldwise conditioning does not condition jointly on all fitted models.
Convergence in probability of the squared L2 root-score difference to a deterministic, potentially misspecified limit, plus positive finite limiting root-score variance.
Integrability for finite-sample unbiasedness; exact assignment alone does not guarantee score stability or useful finite-sample inference.
checked_proof_steps: Applying the arbitrary-Q identity conditional on each training fold establishes conditional and, when integrable, unconditional mean validity.
Conditional variance of the evaluation-fold mean difference equals the squared L2 score difference divided by the fold size.
Conditional Chebyshev with probability bounds truncated at one uses norm convergence in probability without requiring its unconditional expectation to converge.
Fixed-K summation controls the aggregate error without assuming independence across fitted-score folds, yielding asymptotic linearity at the deterministic limiting score.
The iid-root central limit theorem applies to the limiting score under positive finite variance.
Conditional Markov with the same truncation argument gives vanishing empirical mean squared fitted-minus-limit score.
Cauchy-Schwarz, the second-moment law of large numbers and convergence of empirical means establish consistency of the root-score sample variance.
Slutsky then establishes asymptotic Wald coverage, with no quarter-rate Q requirement in this exact-assignment setting.
scope_and_interpretation_checks: The note correctly distinguishes Q-prediction clipping with coherent V recomputation from weight/score clipping.
Misspecified Q does not necessarily achieve efficiency; the theorem asserts neither a universal DR-versus-plug-in variance ordering nor finite-sample coverage.
The 81.25 percent historical coverage is preserved as an empirical finite-replication result, without assigning its cause to Q misspecification.
The empty-cell oracle sensitivity does not verify the new variant confidence intervals or a deployable-method improvement.
The note does not claim that the 80 archived records establish its L2 score-stability condition.
Known assignment, mean validity, asymptotic validity and useful finite-sample precision remain distinct.
remaining_obligations: Applying the theorem to a fitted procedure requires justification of its actual root-score L2 convergence and independent sampling contract.
Prospective finite-sample inference assessment remains outstanding; this review supplies no coverage, efficacy or readiness credit.
basis: Read the completed note and compared its assumptions and proof to the previously reviewed fixed-policy known-assignment argument and main theory section 6.2. Only source hashing and metadata serialization were performed.
